nodes.label: CrySLDoc Correctness Audit
nodes.rationale: Five audit rounds, 85 findings, all fixed and verified at commit 95e0aca. Method deliberately mixes static reading with empirical verification (reflection harnesses, custom .crysl rules, side-by-side builds of git HEAD vs working tree, whole-site link checking, two live 51-rule LLM runs) because 'fixed' and 'proven fixed' are treated as different claims.

nodes.label: C1 - Eleven undocumented behaviour-changing environment variables
nodes.rationale: Eleven env vars silently changed pipeline behaviour with none documented; CRYSLDOC_COMPILE_CHECK=0 disables the compile gate the whole secure-example design rests on. Five were introduced by the audit work itself, which is exactly how the gap formed. Fixed by documenting all thirteen in README rather than removing the tunables, since each has a legitimate operational use.

nodes.label: C2 - Positional list coupling in explanation and code-example loops
nodes.rationale: Same index-pairing shape that produced A1, still present in two more loops. Correct today only by accident of ordering, not by enforced invariant. Fixed by resolving ComposedRule through a Map keyed on class name so the positional invariant is removed rather than merely documented; output byte-identical across 51 pages confirms it was latent.

nodes.label: C3 - populatePredicateTree unguarded lookup and return-instead-of-continue
nodes.rationale: Two latent problems: an unguarded map lookup that would NPE for a predicate no bundled rule ensures, and two `return`s where `continue` is meant, which abandon remaining siblings and leak entries in the shared visitedNodes set, silently truncating later pages' dependency trees. Judged unreachable but still corrected, because the reasoning that makes it safe is not local to the method.

nodes.label: C4 - ComposedRule.llmExplanation never initialised
nodes.rationale: Field is null until the explanation pass sets it, and FreeMarkerWriter reads it without a guard. Safe today because the explanation pass runs on every path including --llm=off, but createSinglePage is a public entry point carrying no such contract. Fixed by initialising to an empty HashMap so the getter is never null regardless of entry point.

nodes.label: B1 - Failed examples publish full Python tracebacks with local absolute paths
nodes.rationale: Five pages published up to 3,344 bytes of traceback, the build machine's absolute paths, and the debug contract dump where a code example should be. Fixed with Utils.summarizeGenerationFailure, which condenses to one publication-safe line preferring the compile-gate verdict plus the first real compiler error and stripping absolute paths; the unabridged text is captured at the catch site into a Full diagnostics section of the failure report so nothing is lost.

nodes.label: B2 - Known-API-mistake rewrite corrupts correct TrustAnchor code
nodes.rationale: A regex meant to repair a model hallucination fired on any two-identifier TrustAnchor call, silently dropping nameConstraints - a real JDK constructor argument and a PKIX security control - while still failing to repair the case it targeted. Removed entirely with a comment recording why: the compile-and-repair loop already handles hallucinated overloads without the risk of silently editing correct code.

nodes.label: B3 - CrySL contract debug dump printed unconditionally
nodes.rationale: Printed to stderr for every rule on every run with no flag guarding it. Because redirectErrorStream merges stderr into the captured output, this dump is what inflates B1's payload - the two findings are the same defect seen from opposite ends. Fixed by gating on CRYSLDOC_DEBUG=1.

nodes.label: B4 - KeyAgreement.crysl aggregates the wrong event label
nodes.rationale: `GenSecretBuffer := gs1 | g2` referenced getInstance instead of gs2, so the published ORDER section told readers a second getInstance call was a valid final protocol step. Found by scanning all 51 rules for defined-but-unreferenced labels - gs2 was the only orphan in the entire set, the signature of exactly this typo. It is a local edit to an upstream-synced rule and must be reported to CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules or it returns on the next sync.

nodes.label: B5 - Dead FTLTemplateLoaderFromJar with getResource().getPath() defect
nodes.rationale: Zero callers; its single method does an unguarded getResource dereference and calls getPath() on a packaged resource, which yields a jar: URL string that is not a usable filesystem path. Third instance of that exact shape after Constant.java (L1) and four Utils methods (N4). Deleted rather than repaired, consistent with the disposition for unreachable code that would need real work to be correct.

nodes.label: A1 - 49 of 51 pages display another class's state-machine diagram
nodes.rationale: createSidebar sorted the caller's composedRuleList in place while createSinglePage paired it positionally against the unsorted cryslRuleList for the diagram. Every other section stayed correct, which made the defect easy to miss and easy to trust. Fixed at both levels - sort a copy, and look the rule up by class name through a Map - because either alone fixes today's symptom but only both remove the class of bug. Verified 51/51 correct, up from 1/51.

nodes.label: A2 - No rule-level failure isolation in the composition loop
nodes.rationale: Zero try/catch in the per-rule composition loop, so one malformed rule aborted the whole 51-rule run after earlier pages were already on disk. Rule loading was resilient; everything downstream was not. Fixed by wrapping the loop body so a throwing rule is added to neither list - preserving the alignment the downstream loops depend on - and reported in a post-loop summary.

nodes.label: A3 - Explanation cache cannot distinguish a real answer from a failure placeholder
nodes.rationale: Cache keyed by class and language with an existence check only, so a disabled-by-flag or error placeholder was served forever. The code-example path already had isRetryablePlaceholder; the explanation path had no equivalent. First fix was incomplete - it corrected the outer reuse decision but LLMService still skipped the call on file existence, rewriting the placeholder with itself. Final fix puts the detector in Utils so both layers share one definition and cannot disagree.

nodes.label: A4 - Compile gate validated against the generator's own classpath
nodes.rationale: javac ran against java.class.path - the full CryptoAnalysis dependency tree - so 'compiles' only proved the example did not reference symbols absent from this project's build, not that a reader could compile it. Fixed to a JDK-only classpath with two opt-in escape hatches rather than hard-coding an exception for the one non-JDK rule. The predicted Cookie regression happened anyway because the hatch was never wired up: predicting a regression is not the same as preventing it.

nodes.label: A5 - Importing llm_utils creates a directory as a side effect
nodes.rationale: A mkdir at module scope meant --help, a syntax check, a unit test or editor autocomplete recreated llm/sanitized_rules/ - including immediately after the N2 cleanup. Removed rather than moved, because the module only ever reads sanitized rules and the Java side already creates the directory before invoking the sidecar. Directory creation belongs in the functions that write files.

nodes.label: A6 - Parameter names string-replaced into diagram labels
nodes.rationale: Labels were built with parameter names then each name globally String.replace'd with its type, so single-letter names like p, q, g corrupted the method name and each substitution corrupted the previous one's output. Found while verifying the A1 fix. Fixed by constructing the label directly from structured parameters so no replacement happens and no corruption is possible.

nodes.label: A7 - Generic parameter types truncated at the last dot
nodes.rationale: substring(lastIndexOf('.')+1) breaks on generics: Set<TrustAnchor> became TrustAnchor> with the outer type lost and a dangling bracket. Fixed with toSimpleTypeName, which shortens every qualified name within the type expression and preserves structure.

nodes.label: N1 - StringEncryption ships in the JAR, crashes, and violates four bundled rules
nodes.rationale: AES/GCM/PKCS5Padding is not a valid transformation in any provider, so the class can never have worked - and it violates four constraints of PBEKeySpec.crysl that this very repository bundles and documents. For a tool generating secure-usage documentation, shipping a compiled example its own rules would reject is a credibility problem independent of the crash. Rewritten to comply rather than deleted, because git history shows it was added deliberately as a user-study example.

nodes.label: N2 - LLM input payload cache is existence-gated
nodes.rationale: Raw payload and sanitized derivative were written only if absent, so when a rule or any sentence generator changed, the model kept being prompted with the previous content. Nothing invalidated it: both directories are gitignored, sit outside target/, and are untouched by the cleanup script. Distinct from A3 - that caches the answer, this caches the question. Fixed by writing both unconditionally, since these are local operations negligible beside the API call that follows.

nodes.label: N3 - System.exit(255) inside library code aborts the whole run
nodes.rationale: An instanceOf constraint whose leaf is neither CrySLPredicate nor CrySLValueConstraint terminated the JVM with no message and an exit code indistinguishable from a CLI usage error. Unreachable with the 51 bundled rules but reachable via a custom --rulesDir rule. Fixed by logging and skipping the clause; the RHS dispatch was also hoisted out of the per-method loop since it is loop-invariant.

nodes.label: N4 - Four dead public Utils methods, one with a latent crash
nodes.rationale: Zero callers anywhere in src/; getConstraintPredicateAndVarnameMap additionally throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on trailing whitespace and matches predicate names with contains(). Deleted along with the four imports they orphaned, same disposition as Constant.java: unreachable code that would need real work to be correct is removed rather than speculatively repaired.

nodes.label: N5 - Cookie JavaDoc link silently lands on an unrelated page
nodes.rationale: Every page linked to the Oracle Java 8 JavaDoc base, but javax.servlet.http.Cookie is Jakarta EE; the URL 302-redirects to the generic JavaSE landing page rather than 404ing, so it fails silently. Fixed by computing the URL once in ClassEventForb.getJavaDocUrl and carrying it on ComposedRule, replacing a base URL hard-coded in two places. A second defect surfaced during the fix: a missing space between rel and href attributes on all 51 pages.

nodes.label: N6 - Markup defects in frontpage.ftl and sidebar.ftl
nodes.rationale: frontpage.ftl put its style block between </head> and <body>; sidebar.ftl had no DOCTYPE so that frame rendered in quirks mode; frontpage.ftl also printed the same sentence twice in adjacent sections. Browsers tolerate the first two, which is why they survived. Fixed, with the duplicated sentence replaced by text that says something different rather than deleted.

nodes.label: N7 - Substring-based variable-to-method matching yields position -1
nodes.rationale: Candidate methods were selected with contains(variableName) then the ordinal computed with indexOf on a whitespace-split signature, so a name that prefixes another matches but resolves to -1. Latent - zero -1 values reached any page. Fixed with a shared FunctionUtils.hasParameterNamed across nine call sites in four classes so selection agrees with the position computation that follows it. Zero output change across 51 pages, exactly as predicted for a latent defect.

nodes.label: N8 - API robustness rested on the SDK's default two retries
nodes.rationale: Not an unprotected pipeline - the SDK defaults to max_retries=2 with backoff - but two retries is not tuned for 204 explanation calls plus up to 102 example calls each looping through 7 repair rounds. Fixed by centralising max_retries=4 and timeout=90s in llm_env.client_kwargs() applied at all eight client constructions, which also avoids widening the duplication the audit already flags.

nodes.label: Golden-output byte-diff regression control
nodes.rationale: Capture all 51 pages, byte-diff after a change. It proved an 18-page blast radius was intended and that latent fixes (N7) changed nothing. But it answers only 'did this change break anything' - it would not have caught A1, A6 or A7, which were wrong before any baseline existed, so every baseline simply enshrined them. Those needed re-deriving expected output from the source rules. It also cannot be extended to the LLM tiers, because model output is not reproducible run to run. It lives in /tmp, not in the repo.

nodes.label: Live-traffic verification - two full 51-rule LLM runs
nodes.rationale: Closed the largest untested surface. OpenAI gpt-4o-mini: 3,649 s, 49/51 secure examples compiling, 0 rate-limit events. Gateway qwen3-30b: 6,836 s, 39/51, one genuine 429 plus five preemptive pauses. Three results inspection could not give: the single 429 was unrecoverable by design because the message carried no 'Limit resets at' timestamp for the backoff helper to parse; all 13 gateway codegen failures published short placeholders rather than broken code; and model output is non-deterministic across runs, so any golden baseline must key on the deterministic tiers only.

nodes.label: Remaining honest verification gaps
nodes.rationale: Ten fixes are compile- and read-verified but never reproduced against real output because no bundled rule exercises their trigger shape, and the live runs cannot change that since they exercise exactly the 51 bundled rules. N2 is proven by inspection, not by a targeted experiment. And no regression baseline exists for the LLM path at all.

nodes.label: Python LLM layer duplication
nodes.rationale: Four copy-pasted client constructions, two copies of make_rag_context, and llm_code_writer_secure.py reimplementing about ten llm_utils.py helpers that have already drifted. Direct evidence of the harm: two same-named helpers with different signatures made a wrong round-3 diagnosis look well supported, and several fixes needed the same edit in multiple places.

nodes.label: Clean bills of health
nodes.rationale: Checked with nothing found: Utils.leafToRootOrderTopo (Kahn with cycle fallback), Utils.extract, gateway_rate_limit.py's sliding window, locking and atomic state write, the reworked EnsuresCaseTwo break binding, and crysl.ftl / header.ftl. Recorded so they are not re-investigated.
